clue.text: Quiet place visited by a group of policemen

parts.note: Pl. is the street-sign abbreviation for Place
the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's plain-clothes detectives

explanation.surface: A peaceful spot suddenly gets a call from a squad of police officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place' shrinks to its address abbreviation, and 'visited by' just puts the detectives after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid describes a calm, untroubled person or scene, a close synonym of quiet.

clue.text: Rope left round beast inside

indicators.note: inside says the animal sits within the ring-shaped letter

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for left
a round shape looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Instructions for tethering an animal: loop the rope round it, leaving the beast inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a looped rope used by cowboys for catching cattle.

clue.text: I torch a clapped-out vehicle

indicators.note: clapped-out means worn out and broken, so the letters fall apart and are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to setting fire to a broken-down old car.
explanation.walkthrough: Clapped-out is British slang for worn out and unreliable, usually said of an old car.
explanation.definitionFit: A chariot is a two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle of ancient warfare and racing.

clue.text: Advance payment is brought over in terminal

indicators.note: brought over suggests flipping the short word end to end
in places the flipped word inside the station word

parts.note: a depot is a bus or rail terminus

explanation.surface: A down payment is handed over at the station.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit is a sum paid up front to secure a purchase, an advance payment by another name.

clue.text: Storyteller getting adult to sit back

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: back tells the solver to read the word for sit in the opposite direction

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: A storyteller persuades a grown-up to settle down and listen.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek teller of fables such as the tortoise and the hare.

clue.text: Sailor, instead, amazingly, went on the wagon

indicators.note: amazingly suggests something astonishing has happened to the word before it, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor, surprisingly, gave up the drink rather than the usual rum.
explanation.walkthrough: Sailors are famed for drinking, which is what makes the surface's surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on the wagon is an idiom for giving up alcohol, which is to abstain.

clue.text: Suppress illegal dealings in game

parts.note: to squash a rebellion is to suppress it

explanation.surface: A call to crack down on crooked dealing in some sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Squash rackets is the full formal name of the indoor racket sport squash.

clue.text: Groom about to be put in prison

indicators.note: put in tells the solver to set one piece inside another

parts.note: pen is US slang for a penitentiary

explanation.surface: A bridegroom is about to be locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' looks like a bridegroom noun, but it is the verb to tidy oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To preen is to groom oneself carefully, as a bird does its feathers.

clue.text: Bubbly does it, and port

indicators.note: bubbly suggests fizzing and churning, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: it is slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: Champagne does the trick, and so does a glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bubbly' and 'port' both look like drinks; one is the anagram signal and the other the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major Black Sea seaport in Ukraine.

clue.text: Terriers, say, having meal in mess

parts.note: terriers are an example of dogs, flagged by say

explanation.surface: Little dogs eating their food make a mess of the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: A dog's breakfast is British slang for a complete muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something botched and chaotic, a mess.

clue.text: A way through unspoilt meadow

indicators.note: through means passing within, so the first pieces go inside the word for unspoilt

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A footpath crosses an untouched field.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasture is grassland for grazing livestock, a meadow.

clue.text: Actress in Oslo as warning broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are strewn and reassembled

explanation.surface: An actress in Norway's capital becomes the subject of a public alert.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloria Swanson was a Hollywood star, famous for Sunset Boulevard.

clue.text: No head for details in book

indicators.note: no head means the word loses its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone without the mind for fine points in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The Acts of the Apostles is a book of the New Testament, usually called Acts.

clue.text: Floor show has nude appearing in kinky act

indicators.note: appearing in places one piece inside the other
kinky means twisted, so the short word is twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A risqué nightclub show features a naked performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabaret is entertainment performed in a nightclub while the audience sits at tables, a floor show.

clue.text: Extraordinary count, rare anecdotalist

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the ordinary, so the letters are taken out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A remarkable, unusual nobleman who loves telling stories.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a skilled teller of stories and anecdotes.

clue.text: First to tackle worker having bizarre fit of bad temper

indicators.note: first to keeps only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker
rum is British slang for odd

explanation.surface: The first person to confront a staff member gets a strange angry outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: A tantrum is an uncontrolled outburst of anger, especially a child's.

clue.text: Fist fight in factory

definitions.meaning: first meaning: old slang for a boxing bout
second meaning: a manufacturing works such as a cotton or paper works

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a punch-up on the shop floor; the boxing sense is old slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a fisticuffs bout in old slang and an industrial works.

clue.text: Client's ordered copy

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so the letters are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A customer has requested a duplicate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' reads as requested, but it signals rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A stencil is a cut-out template used to reproduce a design or lettering, a way to copy.

clue.text: Animal no less uneasy about one

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the numeral
uneasy means unsettled, so the letters are shaken out of order

explanation.surface: An animal that is just as restless about a single thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A lioness is the female lion, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Claimed to be relaxed in examination

indicators.note: relaxed means loosened, so the letters loosen into a different order

explanation.surface: A candidate insists they stayed calm during the test.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical is a physical check-up by a doctor, an examination of health.

clue.text: Wind more vicious round centre of Cadiz

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the word for nastier goes around the kept letter
centre of keeps only the middle letter of the place name

parts.note: the middle letter of the five

explanation.surface: A fiercer gale blows around a Spanish port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' looks like moving air, but it is the verb to twist and turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To meander is to wind or wander along a twisting course, as a river does.

clue.text: The car's passenger, on a trip, is duped?

parts.words: The car's passenger, on a trip
parts.note: surface reading: someone driven somewhere as a passenger on a journey
setter's reading: the same idiom means having been tricked or swindled

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase literally describes a car passenger, and idiomatically someone conned; the question mark flags the double reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being cheated or deceived means exactly duped.

clue.text: Very young child, alone, drops one that's full

indicators.note: drops says the word for solitary sheds the letters of the number

parts.note: taken as written before the cut

explanation.surface: A toddler, left by itself, lets go of the one that is full.
explanation.definitionFit: Total means complete or entire, so full in the sense of utter.

clue.text: Block of gold I obtained around noon

indicators.note: around means the first part encloses the abbreviation

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A miner boasts of acquiring a gold bar at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: The pronoun and the verb together surround the abbreviation, which lands just after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a bar of cast metal, especially gold or silver.

clue.text: Swing component must be put back ahead of rest, we're told

indicators.note: put back says the word for component is written from its end
we're told means as heard, so the second piece is matched by sound not spelling

parts.note: ease means rest; spelt to match the sound

explanation.surface: A piece of a garden swing has to be refitted before you can rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is a horizontal bar hung on ropes, a swing used by acrobats.

clue.text: A synopsis to think over

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a summary of information
second meaning: to absorb and reflect on information

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means a condensed summary; as a verb, to mull over and take in ideas.

clue.text: Following behind leader in race

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Trailing the front-runner in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader in race' paints the front-runner, but it only selects one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Later means coming after in time, so following, as in the following or later chapters.

clue.text: Fairy godmother finally admitted to malice!

indicators.note: admitted to means let inside the word for spite
finally keeps only the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A fairy godmother at last confesses to bearing ill will.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprite is an elf or fairy, a small supernatural being.
